campaign.offer: Kairos Security Total Home Protection Plan: professionally installed home-security systems, with plans starting at $39.99/month and no credit check required. Equipment, installation fees, monitoring and final terms must be confirmed by a specialist; pictured devices are not all included at the starting price.
campaign.audience: Houston-area homeowners and authorized property decision-makers looking for a new system, an upgrade, or help choosing alarm and camera options. Residential needs come first; business inquiries are secondary. These are creative audience hypotheses, not proof of each person's circumstances or exact targeting settings.
campaign.approach: Use Meta ads to introduce the offer, send interested people to the three-question security-options page, capture an inquiry with contact consent, and support specialist follow-up. Ten 4:5 creative designs and matching copy are prepared around distinct reasons to inquire. Qualified conversations and confirmed installations are the goal.

sections.title: Campaign results
sections.body: The campaign recorded 14,912 impressions, reach of 5,674, 357 link clicks and 246 landing page views. Link CTR was 2.39%, link CPC was $2.20 and frequency was 2.63. The campaign targets Houston and surrounding areas with plans starting at $39.99/month.
items: The offer is a starting price. Equipment, installation charges, final pricing and agreement terms require confirmation from a Kairos specialist.
Reported events can include repeat activity or tests. They are not proof of unique qualified inquiries, customers, revenue or profit.

sections.title: What the creative is telling us
sections.body: Product Focus generated 22 of the 24 reported Lead events (91.7%), with $581.14 in spend and a $26.42 cost per result. It received 74.0% of the campaign's spend and is the current observed benchmark, not a proven causal winner.
items: Burgundy Home recorded one Lead event at $13.87; White Houston Home recorded one at $81.73. One-event samples are too small for reliable rankings.
The other six ads had no canonical Lead event reported and received only $4.03-$32.75 each. They are insufficiently tested, not proven failures.

Ten creative assets cover installation, Houston pricing, property fit, monitoring and device options. Prepared creative assets and recommended copy should not be confused with verified live ad settings.
A proposed next test is one fresh product-focused design against the existing benchmark, holding the offer and destination consistent. No campaign changes are authorized by this report.

sections.title: Week-over-week perspective
sections.body: November 5-11 recorded $413.48 in spend, 13 Lead events and $31.81 per result. November 12-18 recorded $371.55 in spend, 11 Lead events and $33.78 per result. Lead cost rose 6.2% while traffic response weakened.
items: Link CTR fell from 3.18% to 1.56%; link CPC rose from $1.69 to $3.29. CPM declined from $53.84 to $51.38.
Frequency declined from 2.39 to 2.10, so ad fatigue is not established. Creative mix, placement mix, attribution and small samples may also explain the change.
These comparisons are observational, not randomized tests. They do not establish that a website change caused better conversion.

sections.title: Audience and placement signals
sections.body: Facebook reported 17 Lead events at $31.66 per result and Instagram reported five at $31.33. Their observed lead costs were similar. Audience Network reported two at $36.22 despite contributing 198 link clicks and 127 landing page views.
items: The 45-54 age group contributed eight Lead events at $24.99 each. This is an early messaging hypothesis, not a reason to exclude other age groups.
The data does not establish which city produces the best lead quality or return. Reconcile city/ZIP, inquiry quality and completed installations before making geographic decisions.
Do not remove placements or change targeting based only on historical segmented costs.

sections.title: The sales follow-up priority
sections.body: The supplied report does not verify an immediate calling process or closed-sale outcomes. Consistent contact and follow-up are the next priorities before increasing ad spend.
items: Proposed interim plan: activate a dedicated business number and have Steve handle first callbacks during agreed coverage hours.
Confirm who owns backup coverage, response-time expectations and follow-up when a prospect cannot be reached.
Have the Kairos specialist confirm equipment, final pricing, service terms and installation before closing.
Track each inquiry through first attempt, reached, qualified, quoted or appointment, won/lost and installed. The proposed process is not a claim that these steps are already operating.

sections.title: Decisions and next steps
sections.body: Prioritize verified sales outcomes before scaling the campaign. Keep the current Product Focus benchmark while evaluating a controlled challenger.
items: Confirm service-area ZIPs, package inclusions, installation availability, fees, agreement length and cancellation terms.
Reconcile the 24 reported events with unique valid inquiries, contact attempts, qualified conversations, quotes and installations.
Agree on a test budget, duration and qualified-lead criteria before changing creative or allocation.
Validate mobile loading and reporting consistency. Some ad-level click counts were inconsistent; reconcile those anomalies before using traffic ratios to make decisions.
Review speed to lead, contact rate, consultations, sales conversion, actual revenue and cost per completed installation weekly.

sections.title: Reporting notes
sections.body: Source: the supplied Kairos Security Complete Marketing, Sales and Campaign Results PDF, dated November 19, 2026. This page is a client-facing summary, not a live dashboard or an independent verification of the underlying account. Main reporting dates are November 5-18 in America/Chicago; attribution may revise prior results.
items: November 19 was a separate partial snapshot: $21.41 spend and one additional Lead event. Combined through that snapshot: $806.44 and 25 events. Do not compare a partial day with completed dates.
The report listed a $1,500 lifetime budget and $693.56 unspent at retrieval. This is historical budget capacity, not a current balance or performance forecast.

The creative-reference portion was prepared without campaign results; the later performance section supplies the dated results summarized here. Prepared recommendations are not evidence of live implementation.
No verified customer, revenue, installation or call-outcome data was supplied. No campaign, budget, targeting, payment or contact settings are changed by this page.
